newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks extend bid deadline for $2-bln thermal plant.
newsitem.headline: Turks extend bid deadline for $2-bln thermal plant.

text.p: Turkey's energy ministry said on Monday the state power authority TEAS had extended the bidding deadline for a $2-billion coal-fired power plant that will produce eight billion kiloWatt-hours of electricity a year.
An energy ministry official said the deadline for the tender for the Afsin-Elbistan plant, in the southeastern Kahramanmaras province, was extended to June 24 from April 29.
"Some foreign companies asked for an extension because some of them were also preparing to bid for our nuclear power plant tender," he told Reuters.
"They are trying to fix their credit lines from international banks," he said.
The plant, to have four generation units each with a capacity of 350 megaWatt (MW), will be similar in output capacity and size as an existing one operating in the same region.
TEAS will use apporpriations from the national budget to finance the plant, officials said.

They said many local companies and several international energy companies including Gec-Altshom, General Electric, Mitsui, Marubeni, ABB, Siemens, Ansaldo, Philipp Holzmann had obtained tender terms and were expected to submit bids.

The area where the plant will be located has lignite coal reserves of 3.5 billion tonnes -- half Turkey's total lignite reserves -- which can supply three more plants that can produce up to 50 billion kWh a year.
